account:
Several people seem to be coordinating something, probably tomorrow's civic presentation of thanks to me, though I have not confirmed that all the activity is connected. The secretary conveyed the innkeeper's request for the great hall tomorrow from 18:00 to 18:30. I approved it. Both the secretary and innkeeper emphasized that preparations finish at 18:00 and I should not arrive earlier. That makes me suspect a surprise is being arranged, rather than ordinary office business.

There is substantial bread-related activity. I noticed freight carrying bread through the great hall this afternoon. The secretary could not establish its purpose and also mentioned reports of the innkeeper carrying bread. This evening I saw the builder give the baker planks and a lantern. I then heard both confirm that materials were full payment for forty-four loaves, replacing an emerald arrangement. The baker promised to deliver them as agreed, but I do not yet know the destination or occasion. My question to the builder went unheard because the builder had left; I have now asked the baker directly and await an answer.

At tea, neighbour mentioned bakery lights and said the baker called them everyday cheer. Neighbour reported no definite dock changes or neighbourhood gatherings. The lights could simply be ordinary bakery work, or could relate to these preparations; I have no proof. The baker had earlier asked about town gatherings needing bread and reported thirty-two loaves stocked for today's sales.

My best guess is that hospitality and tradespeople are preparing a celebratory gathering with bread and decorations, perhaps the presentation tomorrow. The innkeeper, baker and builder appear involved, with the secretary handling the appointment. I have no evidence of wrongdoing or unusual town expenditure: the treasury contained 128 emeralds, and the secretary reported no unusual expenses, although we did not locate account records. It is now just after 19:00, when my appointment book says I should be home.
